title: Microsoft Teams: express face enrollment from meeting video for Teams Rooms recognition
summary: Hold: the licensing model is reported as unpublished even though Microsoft documents the underlying Teams user licence requirement. The roadmap facts and the documented enrollment and room-recognition controls are supported; the remaining uncertainty should be limited to requirements specific to express face enrollment.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; summary; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown because Microsoft has not published a licence for express face enrollment.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included under the standard's rule for a new option inside a licensed product. Replace the unqualified unpublished-licence statements with: 'Teams use requires a Teams licence for each user, except for joining meetings anonymously. Microsoft has not published any licensing requirement or price specific to express face enrollment.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/user-access and https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/teams-service-description. Retain the separately stated Teams Rooms Pro requirement for room recognition, and narrow the summary, licensing notes and cost rationale to say that feature-specific licensing is not yet published rather than that the underlying entitlement is unknown.
